front.title: Verifiable AI Provenance Framework (VAP): An Architectural Framework for Auditable AI Decision Trails

abstract.t:
Automated decision-making systems, including AI and algorithmic systems in critical infrastructure, currently lack standardized mechanisms for producing provenance records that third parties can verify independently. Traditional logging approaches do not provide the cryptographic properties that regulatory examination, forensic investigation, and cross-organizational accountability depend on: detectability of alteration, detectability of omission after commitment, and attribution.
This document describes the Verifiable AI Provenance Framework (VAP), an architectural framework that defines requirements for producing verifiable decision trails using existing IETF security technologies. VAP does not define new protocols or cryptographic primitives; rather, it provides an architectural coordination layer that enables domain-specific profiles to leverage Supply Chain Integrity, Transparency and Trust (SCITT), Remote Attestation Procedures (RATS), CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE), and related IETF work in a consistent manner.
VAP makes records auditable and attributable after the fact. It does not prevent, block, or intercept any system behaviour, and it does not warrant that any recorded decision was correct, fair, or safe. The detailed requirement set is maintained by the VeritasChain Standards Organization (VSO) as a separate specification; this document describes the architecture and its mapping to IETF work.
This document is intended to frame the problem space and facilitate discussion about whether architectural coordination work is needed in this area.
